family.tagline: Two studios under one roof, and one Core in the study.
family.story: Elias photographs families and small businesses. Mika is an operations consultant. Both work from home in a white house by the canal, and their clients' files live on one Companion Core.

companion.name: Marlo
companion.job: Opens Twenty and other web pages in its own browser and fills in the forms Elias asks for.
companion.limits: One task at a time. Elias checks every result.

companion.name: Odette
companion.job: Drafts replies and answers questions for Mika's clients, using the context she connected.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Mika reads and sends every message.

popup.title: The parcel arrives
popup.body: Mika finds a parcel on the doorstep after a morning call. Elias carries it through the foyer and the dining room to her study, where the desk is cleared.

popup.title: What is in the parcel
popup.body: Elias opens it. Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Its footprint is about three quarters of a sheet of paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Mika plugs in the power cable and presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: A phone joins the Core
popup.body: Elias joins the Core's own Wi-Fi from his phone. Then he picks the home network and types its password.

popup.title: First agents, first apps
popup.body: In Companion Hub, Mika picks Hermes and Elias picks OpenClaw. They add Immich, Twenty and Paperless-ngx, plus Companion Memory (beta). Then they walk away.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Odette says hello
popup.body: Mika sends her first message. Odette, the agent she named, answers.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: mika
say.text: Hello, Mika. I am Odette. Where should we begin?

beats.capability: Back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Thursday's portraits, sorted
popup.body: Elias sorts Thursday's portrait session into an Immich album from the couch. When the clients ask where their photos live, the answer is the Core, in this house.

beats.capability: Stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Friday film night, from the Core
popup.body: Mika chooses the film. Jellyfin plays her own collection on the living-room TV, straight from the Core.

beats.capability: Track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: Groceries, planned together
popup.body: Mika drafts the week's shopping list in Grocy at the breakfast bar. When Elias adds oat milk on his phone, it lands on the same list.

beats.capability: a recipe book and an expiry tracker for the household

popup.title: The fridge has an expiry list
popup.body: Elias logs the new cheese in the HomeHub expiry tracker, standing at the fridge. Now the whole household can see what to eat first.

beats.capability: Track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: Every plan, in one list
popup.body: Elias opens Wallos at the counter. It lists the gallery and storage plans he still pays for, with a reminder before each one renews. He cancels the old ones himself.

beats.capability: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Odette drafts, Mika decides
popup.body: A client asks which week suits a workshop. Odette drafts the reply from context Mika connected to Companion Memory. Mika sends it herself.

say.speaker: mika
say.text: Draft ready. Please read it before it goes anywhere.

popup.title: A signed scope, filed once
popup.body: Mika scans a client's signed scope of work. Paperless-ngx reads every page, tags it and files it, so one search finds it later.

beats.capability: Track time per project and client, with reports

popup.title: Hours counted per client
popup.body: Mika logs her consulting hours in Kimai, project by project. At month end, a report for each client is ready on the Core.

beats.capability: Back up your files with encryption before they leave your Core

popup.title: A second copy of every shoot
popup.body: On a schedule, Duplicati backs up the client folders to a local disk. The files are encrypted before they are written.

beats.capability: Keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

popup.title: Marlo logs a new enquiry
popup.body: A wedding enquiry arrives. Marlo opens Twenty in its own browser and adds the lead. Elias checks every field.

say.speaker: elias
say.text: Lead drafted. Please check each field.

beats.capability: Design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: An album, laid out at home
popup.body: Elias lays out a family album in Penpot, a web-based design tool hosted on the Core. Each spread comes together in his browser.

beats.capability: A file server with media player, search and Markdown editor in the browser

popup.title: Every client has a folder
popup.body: Each client gets a folder in copyparty, the file server on the Core. Elias searches and browses the day's selects from his laptop.

beats.capability: Send files between phones and laptops on the same Wi-Fi

popup.title: Phone to laptop, over the Wi-Fi
popup.body: After a location shoot, Elias sends test frames from his phone to his laptop with PairDrop. They travel over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: A PDF toolkit that runs in your browser

popup.title: Plan and quote, one file
popup.body: Elias assembles a shoot plan and a quote into one PDF in BentoPDF, a toolkit that runs in his browser. He checks every page before it goes out.

beats.capability: A local video recorder with object detection for your IP cameras

popup.title: The carport, recorded at home
popup.body: An IP camera over the carport streams to Frigate. The recordings stay on the Core, and the clips play on the home network.

beats.capability: Plan, map and share hiking and biking routes from GPX files

popup.title: Sunday's ride, planned at home
popup.body: Mika plans Sunday's towpath ride in Wanderer from a GPX file. The route and the map stay on the Core.

beats.capability: Stream your own music from your Core to a browser or an app

popup.title: Records by the canal
popup.body: Elias plays his own records from mStream on the patio, streamed from the Core to a browser on his phone.

popup.title: Two studios, one Core
popup.body: Two studios, one canal and one Companion Core. The Vance-Takahashi household keeps its clients' files in the study.

closing.body: Keep your clients' folders, your paperwork and your agents on a Companion Core at home. When someone asks where the files live, you can point at the desk.

notes: FTUE follows the owner-specified hotspot flow; the fact sheet says only "plug it in, pair it over Wi-Fi, and walk away". Owner sign-off open.
Apps chosen to leave the busiest store apps to other families: Grocy, Duplicati (a local disk), copyparty, BentoPDF, Wanderer, mStream. PairDrop is described as Wi-Fi file transfer only.
Motif: where the clients' files live. Beats living-couch, study-backup, studio-files, closing. No legal claim about client photos is made.
garden-cameras assumes the family owns an IP camera over the carport: it is not in the Core parcel and not in the 3D scene. It records the family property only.
Desk anchors: desk:office nth 0 is meant to be the ground-floor study and nth 1 the upstairs editing room; story-bake should confirm the order.
